articles.title: Police to escort fire crews in latest crackdown on Bonfire Night disorder
articles.summary: As many as 1,700 officers could be deployed in the biggest Police Scotland operation since last year's visit by President Trump.
articles.body:
Police officers are to be embedded in fire stations and will travel with crews to tackle potential attacks on firefighters during Bonfire Night.

The move is part of Scotland's biggest police operation since the visit of President Donald Trump last summer and a response to a "unique" combination of safety concerns.

As many as 1,700 officers could be deployed to deal with fireworks-related disorder, a European football match involving Celtic and potential protests in Glasgow.

Additional public order vehicles and drivers are being brought in from 18 English and Welsh police forces under mutual aid arrangements.

Emergency services have long recommended organised displays as the safest and often most impressive way of enjoying fireworks.

Where can I watch an organised fireworks display?

Many of the large council-run Bonfire Night events once held across Scotland have disappeared over recent decades because of cost pressures, including insurance, security and stewarding, as well as the complexity of organising large public events.

Glasgow has not held a display at Glasgow Green since before Covid in 2019 and the council-run Bonfire Night display at Edinburgh's Meadowbank Stadium was last held in 2017.

Many clubs and private venues, however, continue to host organised displays throughout Scotland.

According to the Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) around 20 organised fireworks displays have taken place across Scotland in the last five days with a further 79 planned.

Scotland's annual public order operation for Halloween and Bonfire Night, known as Operation Moonbeam, is now in its ninth year.

The operation has grown in scale over the years, particularly since an upsurge of disorder in 2023 which left 62 officers injured.

The worst violence occurred in the Niddrie area of Edinburgh where groups of youths attacked officers with fireworks, petrol bombs and other missiles.

Glasgow and Dundee have also seen significant disorder in recent years, and emergency workers have frequently been targeted.

This year a new initiative, Operation Amberlight, will see police officers based at fire stations in certain areas to better protect emergency crews.

Glasgow and the surrounding area is a particular focus, with police officers working out of 10 fire stations across Glasgow, East Dunbartonshire and East Renfrewshire.

Supt Ross Aitken said: "It's to provide support to fire service colleagues.

"Should they come under attack then the police officers will be there to support them.

"But it's also just to provide an effective and efficient response to any incidents that may occur."

He added: "The vast majority of the public act in a responsible and safe manner, but to the small minority who are intent on engaging in anti-social behaviour and other criminality - we will adopt a robust response to you."

Since 2024 Fireworks Control Zones (FCZs), which ban the use of pyrotechnics in certain areas, have been used in known troublespots, first in Edinburgh and then in Glasgow the following year.

Under the restrictions, it is a criminal offence to set off a firework within the FCZ boundary or throw one into a zone.

SFRS Commander Mark Cleland said: "If you look at the incident stats over the last few years there's certainly been benefit from the fireworks control zones.

"And there's been an increase in control zones from 12 to 18 this year so hopefully we will see a further reduction in antisocial behaviour within these zones."

Last year, the fire service took around 750 calls on Bonfire Night and attended more than 250 bonfires.

Between 31 October and 5 November 2025, police said just over 830 calls needed a local or specialist response.

But that figure was down by more than a third on the previous year.

Cleland said: "For firefighters we have dealt with anti-social behaviour on occasions, it tends to be the minority but what we want is our personnel and our staff who are out on Thursday night to ensure that they go home safely to their families.

"They are mums, dads, brothers and sisters just the same as everybody else in the community and we really want our crews to make it home safe."

So far this year, there has been a modest decrease in fireworks-related calls to police on Halloween.

A total of 144 were received on Saturday night, down from 160 in 2025.

But there have been more serious incidents, including one where a firework landed near a pram in the Drumchapel area of Glasgow, leaving a child badly shaken.

And in Bonnyrigg, Midlothian, there were reports of fireworks being thrown in the high street.

Two male youths have since been charged.

On Tuesday police seized 350kg of fireworks worth about £12,000 from an address in the Penilee area of Glasgow.

Officers said they were being sold online, with some having the capacity to fire 600 individual rockets.

This year's Bonfire Night operation will see police coping with two further challenges, both in Scotland's biggest city.

Celtic will take on Turkish side Besiktas in a Uefa Europa League match at Celtic Park, which kicks off at 20:00.

Officers say they are also aware of images circulating online, suggesting "planned protest activity" will also take place in Glasgow the same night.

Supt Aitken said: "So that intelligence picture just continues to develop and that will be fed into the planning team so that we can adapt our response.

"There are a number of competing events that are going to take place on Thursday.

"But I can give that assurance that we have proportionate policing plans in place to deal with that."

Animal welfare organisations regularly highlight the distress fireworks can cause to pets, livestock and wildlife.

Two years ago Edinburgh Zoo said a three-month-old red panda called Roxie had probably died from stress linked to Bonfire Night fireworks.

The zoo now falls within a firework control zone, which it welcomed as a positive step forward.

Ben Supple, deputy chief executive of the Royal Zoological Society of Scotland which runs the zoo, said this was only part of the solution.

"Ahead of Bonfire Night, we would ask members of the public to be mindful of the impact fireworks can have on animals and to avoid setting them off near the zoo or in areas where they may cause distress to wildlife and pets," he said.

The Scottish SPCA has called for a UK-wide ban on the private sale and use of fireworks, and a 90 decibel noise limit as an interim measure, down from the current 120db limit.

The charity advises pet owners to keep animals inside after dark, closing windows doors and curtains, and having music playing or the TV on during a nearby display.

articles.title: Quentin Tarantino and Kylie Minogue film movie in Porthcawl
articles.summary: A Hollywood giant and singing superstars caused a stir after arriving in a Welsh seaside town.
articles.body:
Sharing a pint with Reservoir Dogs and Pulp Fiction director Quentin Tarantino in his local pub was a surreal experience for a Welsh filmmaker.

But this was just the tip of the iceberg for Jamie Adams, who also managed to get singing icon Kylie Minogue and rapper RZA from the Wu-Tang Clan to Porthcawl for his new movie.

The arrival of the stars in the seaside town earlier this year to work on Tangled Up in Blue caused a buzz, and Adams admitted it felt like "an out of body experience" bringing his heroes to his hometown.

It is not the first time he has brought big names to south Wales, having worked with Dirty Dancing star Jennifer Grey on 2019 film Bittersweet Symphony.

Adams was able to include scenes in locations that mean a lot to him, including the pub his dad used to run.

"It was called the Ship and Castle then and the bar is actually a boat that he brought from Weymouth, which is where I was born," he said.

"So I've got Quentin Tarantino having a pint with me in my dad's old pub, talking to Neil, one of my old pals, who I've known since I was like eight years old.

Tangled Up in Blue follows a talent manager (Tarantino) who has spent 40 years managing legends but finds himself stranded at a hotel bar caught between an old flame and a lost soul.

It all fell into place with the involvement of the superstars after Adams filmed in France last year.

He shot a movie there in a week in his usual improv style - which is where much of it is created spontaneously rather than being read from a pre-written script.

Adams said Tarantino thoroughly enjoyed it, and described it as reminding him of French New Wave cinema that emerged from the late 1950s to the late 1960s.

"I said [to him] I'd love to do one that was a little bit more personal to me, and actually shot in in my hometown," Adams added.

Getting Minogue, who has described herself as "half Welsh" to be part of the project was even easier.

Her family actually hail from near Porthcawl, with mum Carol Jones and her Welsh-speaking Nain Millie Jones emigrating from Maesteg, also in Bridgend county, to Australia in the 1950s.

Despite these strong roots in the country, she told Adams she was rarely able to visit, so jumped at the chance.

The filmmaker likened the project to a small football team going on a cup run, saying it "brought people together in the story".

He explained: "They're still talking about it down my local pub.

"It's like there's still people that would stop me and kind of want to talk about their favourite Tarantino film or Kylie's records.

"I'm sure one day, I'll have time to sit down and actually think about it all properly.

"At the moment, it just feels like this beautiful haze that is the heart of this film."

Adams said it felt right to do most of the filming in Wales' capital Cardiff and his hometown for what was such a personal movie.

He also loved the process of showing what his star cast is capable of but not necessarily known for.

Tarantino is better known for his work behind the camera, while Minogue has become one of the world's most famous pop stars after leaving Australian soap Neighbours in the late 1980s.

Adams also liked the fact his improv approach gave them freedom over their characters in a way that might not be possible on other productions.

While there is no current release date, the director is aiming for summer 2027.

He also hopes Cardiff can play host to a premiere, with his star cast attending.

"I think you've got to be very grateful that you were able to work with them," he added.

"It was about bringing a spirit a joy to south Wales."

articles.title: MS NOW host suggests Byron Donalds’ not true 'kinfolk' after historic Florida gubernatorial victory
articles.summary: MS NOW host Symone Sanders Townsend appeared to suggest Florida Gov.-elect Byron Donalds wasn't true "kinfolk" with other Black Americans because of his conservative policies.
articles.body: MS NOW host Symone Sanders Townsend suggested Tuesday that Florida Republican Byron Donalds wasn't true "kinfolk" with other Black Americans after acknowledging his historic victory in the state's race for governor. Sanders Townsend questioned the political significance of Donalds' victory, saying he would continue Gov. Ron DeSantis' agenda. "I will say, though, you know, as they say in my community, all kinfolk ain’t skinfolk," Sanders Townsend said, although she appeared to mean it the other way around. "And what I say and what I mean by that is Byron Donalds is making history, but he is going to continue the political direction that Ron DeSantis is going to continue in Florida." FLORIDA GOV-ELECT DONALDS BELIEVES 'FRUSTRATIONS BOILED OVER' AGAINST REPUBLICANS ON ELECTION DAY Tim Graham, Media Research Center director of media analysis and executive editor of NewsBusters, criticized the remarks in a statement to Fox News Digital, saying Sanders Townsend was suggesting Black conservatives’ political beliefs conflicted with their racial identity. "Symone Sanders is trying to argue that Blackness and conservatism are polar opposites or that being a Black conservative is being a traitor to your race," Graham said. "She suggests that Gov. Ron DeSantis has been anti-Black in his policies, and so Donalds is going to continue this allegedly anti-Black agenda." Graham compared the criticism to Democrats' treatment of Clarence Thomas during his difficult 1991 Supreme Court confirmation hearings, when Thomas described the proceedings as a "high-tech lynching." Graham said the underlying message demanded political conformity from Black Americans. CLARENCE THOMAS SCORCHES RACIAL LITMUS TESTS POLICING THOUGHT: ‘STAY BLACK AND DIE’ Sanders Townsend's comments followed Donalds' narrow victory over Democrat David Jolly in the state. Donalds will succeed term-limited DeSantis in a rare bright spot for Republicans Tuesday, after Democrats swept into power across the rest of the country. Sanders Townsend explicitly acknowledged the significance of Donalds’ election before turning to his policies and comparing his agenda to the outgoing governor’s. "It is a historic win. It is the first time Florida has elected a Black governor," Sanders Townsend said. "And, so, he was on ‘The Breakfast Club’ this morning, was being asked about all kinds of policies and whatnot. And he, you know, sounded similar to Ron DeSantis." FIRST MUSLIM SENATOR, FIRST BLACK FEMALE GOVERNOR: 2026 MIDTERM ELECTION RESULTS MAKE HISTORY Donalds previously pushed back against Rep. Jasmine Crockett, D-Texas, after she criticized his marriage to a White woman in remarks that resurfaced in 2025. Speaking on "The Joe Pags Show," Donalds said his wife should be left out of their political dispute. "Here’s what I’m going to say, first and foremost: Don’t talk about my wife. Keep my wife out of this. It ain’t got nothing to do with her," Donalds said. articles.title: Immigration debate tone may change
articles.summary: BENGALURU: A Democratic majority in Congress may shift the tone of the US immigration debate, but it is unlikely to bring immediate policy relief for
articles.body: BENGALURU: A Democratic majority in Congress may shift the tone of the US immigration debate, but it is unlikely to bring immediate policy relief for Indian technology professionals or employers.Experts believe a Democratic victory could help temper anti-immigrant sentiment and the political rhetoric targeting Indian technology professionals, creating a more favourable environment for skilled immigration and potentially laying the groundwork for policy changes in the longer term.Stephen Yale-Loehr, retired professor of immigration law practice at Cornell Law School, said a change in congressional control would not immediately translate into immigration reform."President Trump is still president, and he controls the immigration agencies. Even if the Democrats pass positive immigration laws, President Trump can veto them. However, the Democrats can hold hearings and investigations to try to persuade the US public that immigration benefits, not hurts, the country. That way they will lay the groundwork for possible true immigration reform in 2029, assuming the Democrats control Congress then and there is a Democratic president then," he said.David J Bier, director of Immigration Studies at Cato Institute, echoed this assessment, saying the election outcome would have almost no immediate impact on immigration policy. "It will have almost no immediate effect because Republicans still have enough votes to block most immigration bills in the Senate, and even if they didn't, Trump would veto bills that block his agenda," he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Kevin Bacon’s charity brought more than 100 volunteers to a Virginia campus; together they assembled 35,000 meal kits and 400 mental health kits for students and families across the region
articles.summary: A few hours of volunteering can make a difference long after an event ends, particularly for families struggling to afford food and students dealing with
articles.body: A few hours of volunteering can make a difference long after an event ends, particularly for families struggling to afford food and students dealing with emotional challenges. More than 100 volunteers came together at George Mason University in Virginia for an initiative that combined food assistance with mental health support, assembling thousands of meal kits and hundreds of resource kits for people across the region.The event was organised by SixDegrees.org, the nonprofit founded by actor Kevin Bacon, in partnership with George Mason University. According to the university's Office of the Provost, which published details of the initiative on July 29, 2026, the volunteers gathered on the university's Fairfax Campus on July 19 for a special edition of the organisation's Building Kits by Kevin Bacon programme. Their collective effort produced 35,000 meal kits for students and families across Northern Virginia and 400 mental health kits for George Mason students.How the initiative supported students and familiesThe meal kits were intended to address food insecurity, a challenge that can affect families as well as university students. The partnership developed following discussions about George Mason's Patriot Pantry, a campus resource that provides food assistance to students facing financial difficulties. Stacy Huston, chief executive officer of SixDegrees.org, said the university's existing work supporting students made it a natural partner for the initiative.Most of the 35,000 meal kits were scheduled for distribution through Food for Others, a nonprofit organisation serving Fairfax County. Some of the kits were also set aside for George Mason's Patriot Pantry so students could access assistance directly on campus. The partnership brought together university faculty and staff, alumni, community members and local nonprofit organisations. Rather than limiting the activity to donations, the organisers involved volunteers in preparing the supplies that would eventually reach people who needed them.Mental health kits offered encouragement and supportAlongside food assistance, volunteers assembled 400 mental health kits in partnership with Find Your Anchor, an organisation focused on suicide prevention and emotional support. The kits included practical resources, encouraging messages and information intended to help people experiencing emotional distress. They were designed to remind recipients that they were not alone and encourage them to seek additional support when needed.George Mason planned to distribute the kits to students throughout the year during mental health, well-being and suicide prevention awareness events. Rachel Wernicke, the university's chief mental health officer, said the initiative complemented its broader suicide prevention efforts. She highlighted the importance of providing hope and reminding people affected by suicide that support is available.The two types of kits addressed different but connected needs. While meal packages offered practical assistance to people facing food insecurity, mental health kits provided resources and encouragement for students dealing with emotional difficulties.Partnership also includes research on community well-beingThe collaboration between SixDegrees.org and George Mason University extends beyond the volunteer event. Global and community health professor Ali Weinstein is working with the nonprofit on a research project examining how providing tangible forms of support affects both recipients and volunteers. The research will explore whether activities such as distributing mental health kits can influence the well-being of people receiving assistance as well as those participating in the volunteer work.George Mason President Gregory Washington said the partnership reflected the university's commitment to student well-being beyond academic performance. Vice President for University Life Rose Pascarell also highlighted how cooperation between universities and community organisations can strengthen relationships and encourage community engagement. Kevin Bacon, who founded SixDegrees.org in 2007, thanked the volunteers for their contribution during the event. He described their collective effort with the words, "Action is hope." Huston said she hoped the collaboration would encourage other communities and organisations to develop similar initiatives.The July event demonstrated how a university, a nonprofit organisation and local volunteers could combine their efforts to address food insecurity and mental health needs. With 35,000 meal kits and 400 mental health kits prepared in a single activation, the partnership aimed to provide practical support while building stronger connections across Northern Virginia.You use AI every day. articles.title: SC: Can't become third chamber of Parliament
articles.summary: 'Can't interfere in norms for SC/ST seats in house' NEW DELHI: Refusing to blur the constitutional 'Lakshman Rekha' that separates the three organs of
articles.body: 'Can't interfere in norms for SC/ST seats in house'NEW DELHI: Refusing to blur the constitutional 'Lakshman Rekha' that separates the three organs of governance, Supreme Court Wednesday said it cannot usurp legislature's exclusive powers to interfere in the criteria for reserving an assembly or parliamentary constituency for Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes."We cannot become the third chamber of Parliament," a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said while refusing to entertain a petition seeking quashing of a notification reserving Kadipur assembly constituency in UP for SCs.The CJI-led bench said identification of constituencies to reserve them for SCs or STs was the sole prerogative of the legislature and the court could not interfere in it, and suggested the petitioner could resort to protests to make elected representatives take corrective measures.The bench, which has been dealing with a large number of petitions on CJP protests, said in a lighter vein, "It is a good season for protest, dharna and 'naare baji'. You can also raise your voice (in protest) and tell the elected representatives that time is ripe for revising the criteria of reserving constituencies for the SC community and adopt the principle of rotational reservation. By approaching the constitutional court, you have dialled a wrong number."Appearing for a petitioner, senior advocate Gagan Gupta questioned the manner in which constituencies were geographically identified and reserved for SCs and asked whether "Section 9(1)(c) of the Delimitation Act, 2002, can constitutionally operate in a manner which permits the same territorial constituencies to remain reserved for SCs over successive electoral cycles without any mechanism for periodic rotation".The bench said, "Delimitation is a legislative exercise and the guidelines for carrying out that exercise cannot be tweaked by the courts. Can the judiciary mandate the Delimitation Commission to adopt rotational reservation policy while demarcating constituencies for SCs?"The SC agreed with Allahabad HC, which had said that since Articles 330 and 332 provide for reserving constituencies for SCs and STs, no general candidate could claim that his right to contest from constituencies reserved for SCs and STs was violated.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
